title: m.iMX RT: After a few seconds print() hangs
body: On my Teensy 4.1, simple_benchmarks.py hangs, and I reduced it to a timing and printing problem. A print during each iteration lets the program finish, but allowing it to run for several seconds without printing causes the final print to hang. Even this reproduces it: print 'Start..', sleep for 5 seconds, then print 'Finish'. It is only a question of duration: after more than about 4 seconds the print hangs. I am using MicroPython v1.19.1-782-g699477d12 on a Teensy 4.1 with MIMXRT1062DVJ6A.

symptoms_visible: On my Teensy 4.1, a final print and return to the REPL hang if the program runs quietly for more than about four seconds.
Printing a dot at intervals lets the benchmark run through, while a five-second sleep before printing 'Finish' reproduces the problem.
N0.label: N0 delayed output hang reported

symptoms_visible: In the five-second test, the LED turns on and then turns off after five seconds, but 'Finish' does not appear and the USB REPL does not return.
Omitting the final print does not restore the REPL; Ctrl-D still causes a soft reboot.
N1.label: N1 program execution continues

symptoms_visible: When the REPL is duplicated to UART, the serial connection receives 'Finish' and the prompt after the long test, while the USB terminal does not.
Pressing Enter in the stalled USB terminal can bring back a prompt without the missing 'Finish' output.
A several-second loop using a preallocated array produces the same USB-only stall without consuming additional memory.
N2.label: N2 failure isolated to USB channel

symptoms_visible: The same Teensy and five-second test work normally on a Windows 10 laptop, but the USB output stalls on my Manjaro Linux NUC.
The full benchmark also runs to completion when the board is connected to the Windows 10 machine.
N3.label: N3 host dependency established

symptoms_visible: After I disabled USB autosuspend on my Manjaro system, the delayed print and USB REPL work normally and the problem is gone.
N4.label: N4 host setting identified and tested

symptoms_visible: The five-second test prints 'Finish', returns to the USB REPL, and the benchmark completes on the affected Linux machine.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Can you toggle an LED around the delay to determine whether execution stops or only the output disappears?
Please add a hardware-visible action after the long delay and report whether it occurs when the terminal appears stuck.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I added an LED. In test2 it works normally. In test5 the LED switches on and, after five seconds, switches off, but 'Finish' is not printed. It still reacts to Ctrl-D with a soft reboot.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The LED never switches off after the five-second delay, and Ctrl-D has no effect.
The LED switches off after six seconds rather than exactly five, but the output is still absent.

edges.comment: The LED probe from c2-c4 shows that Python execution reaches the code after the delay even though output and the USB REPL appear stuck. The reporter also volunteered that removing the final print does not restore the prompt.

question_patterns: Can you duplicate the REPL to a hardware UART and compare what appears there with the USB terminal during the same test?
Please run the delayed test with an independent serial output channel and report the output visible on each channel.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I used os.dupterm with UART6. Even when I start test5 from USB and the second print hangs there, 'Finish' is printed on the serial connection and the REPL prompt returns there. On USB it remains stalled; pressing Enter can return a prompt while omitting 'Finish'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both UART and USB stop before 'Finish', and neither connection returns to the prompt.
UART receives 'Finish' slightly later than expected, but USB still receives nothing until I press Enter.

question_patterns: Does sending any input on the stalled USB terminal change what you see?
When USB output stalls, what happens if you press Enter?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: An Enter keypress in the USB terminal can make the >>> prompt reappear, but the final 'Finish' text is still missing.

edges.comment: The UART comparison in c21-c23 isolates the visible failure to the USB channel. The reporter's preallocated-array test also reproduces it without ongoing allocation, separating it from the distinct memory-management assertions discussed earlier.

question_patterns: Which host operating system shows the problem, and can you test the same board and script on another computer?
Does the behavior follow the Teensy when you connect it to a different host?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My affected computer is a NUC running Manjaro Linux. I tried the same Teensy on my son's Windows 10 laptop, and test5 has no problem there. The benchmark also runs to completion on Windows 10.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same board stalls identically on Manjaro, Windows 10, and another Linux computer.
It works on a different Linux laptop as well as Windows, but still fails on my Manjaro NUC.

edges.comment: The alternate-host test in c25-c27 shows that the symptom follows the affected PC environment rather than the Teensy firmware alone.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the affected host's services, power-management settings, and logs for anything that acts on an idle ttyACM device, change one relevant setting, and rerun the test?
Please compare the affected host's USB behavior and background services with the working host, then report which host-side change affects the result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: USB autosuspend was the culprit on my PC. I disabled it at boot on Manjaro and the problem is now gone.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I disabled the relevant host USB power management and rebooted, but test5 still stalls in exactly the same way.
Disabling the setting only for this USB device fixes it; disabling it globally also works.
The working laptop uses a different terminal font and keyboard layout.

edges.comment: In c32-c33 the maintainer asked about host power saving and the reporter identified USB autosuspend, disabled it persistently, and reported that the problem disappeared.

solution.intent: Treat the apparent MicroPython print hang as a host-side Linux USB autosuspend problem: keep autosuspend disabled or exempt the Teensy CDC device, then verify the delayed print and benchmark through USB.
solution.concrete_example: Disable USB autosuspend on the affected Manjaro host, or configure a device-specific exemption for the Teensy USB CDC device. Reconnect or reboot as required, then rerun test5 and simple_benchmarks.py over USB and confirm that 'Finish' and the REPL prompt appear without periodic keepalive prints.
solution.inference_hint: The evidence establishes that execution continues, UART output succeeds, the behavior depends on the host, and disabling Linux USB autosuspend removes it. Interpreting these observations as an idle host power-management interruption of the USB CDC path is the diagnostic inference; it is not evidence that the Python VM or print implementation stopped.

edges.comment: Final accepted resolution from c33-c34: host USB autosuspend was the culprit. Later discussion about TinyUSB callbacks did not replace this accepted diagnosis.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as USB autosuspend on the affected Manjaro Linux host, not a Python timing, sleep, floating-point, garbage-collection, or general print failure.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the LED proves execution continues, UART receives the missing output and prompt while USB stalls, the same board works on Windows 10, and disabling USB autosuspend removes the problem.
Must recommend disabling host USB autosuspend or exempting the Teensy USB CDC device rather than relying on periodic print calls as the permanent workaround.
Must not conflate the separate allocation-related assertion failures discussed during investigation with this no-allocation, USB-only delayed-output issue.
Must have the reporter verify both the delayed print test and normal benchmark output over USB after the host-side change before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable embedded MicroPython user who can reduce test cases, wire an LED and FTDI serial adapter, configure UART REPL duplication, install firmware, and change Linux power-management settings.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent, exploratory, and evidence-driven; provides complete test programs and detailed observations, questions competing hypotheses, and willingly runs hardware and host-comparison experiments.
